references.text: God will enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem. This is the blessing over Japheth as the father of the nations mentioned in Genesis 10:2.
A direct parallel listing the sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras – identical to Genesis 10:2.
Gog from the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, is mentioned in the prophecy. Magog, Meshech, and Tubal are all sons of Japheth.
Javan, Tubal, and Meshech are mentioned as traders. These are among the sons of Japheth and show their role among the nations.
Mentions Meshech, who is one of the sons of Japheth in Genesis 10:2, in a context of a foreign land.
Mentions Tubal and Javan among distant peoples, both of whom are sons of Japheth mentioned in Genesis 10:2.
Gog and Magog are mentioned in an eschatological context. Magog is one of the sons of Japheth, and the name is used here for hostile nations in the end times.
Directly expands the genealogy by listing descendants of the first son mentioned (Gomer) in the source verse.
Directly expands the genealogy by listing descendants of another son (Javan) mentioned in the source verse.
Places Japheth's line within the broader context of Noah's three sons, showing the parallel structure of the post-flood genealogy.
Expands the genealogy to Shem's branch, providing a complete overview of the distribution of Noah's grandchildren parallel to Japheth's line.
